question: Express the matrix $M = \begin{bmatrix}0 & a & b \\ -a & 0 & c \\ -b & -c & 0\end{bmatrix}$ as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix.
explanation:
Let $S = \frac{1}{2}(M + M')$ and $K = \frac{1}{2}(M - M')$.

But $M'$ (transpose): $M' = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -a & -b \\ a & 0 & -c \\ b & c & 0\end{bmatrix}$

$S = \frac{1}{2}(M + M') = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 & a-a & b-b \\ -a+a & 0 & c-c \\ -b+b & -c+c & 0\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$

$K = \frac{1}{2}(M - M') = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 & a-(-a) & b-(-b) \\ -a-a & 0 & c-(-c) \\ -b-b & -c-c & 0\end{bmatrix}$

$=\frac{1}{2} \begin{bmatrix}0 & 2a & 2b \\ -2a & 0 & 2c \\ -2b & -2c & 0\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}0 & a & b \\ -a & 0 & c \\ -b & -c & 0\end{bmatrix}$

So,

$M = 0 + M$ (i.e., $M$ is purely skew-symmetric).
